criteria.statement: On the aged fixture, one `--rebase` call restores the missing framework file, lists it under `added`, and the restored file is byte-identical to the plugin's copy
criteria.evidence: Transcript of the `--rebase` run (plugin dir `packages/full`) showing the `REBASE_RESULT` line with the path in its category's `added`; `cmp` of the restored file against the plugin's rendered copy exiting 0

criteria.statement: On the aged fixture, the previously-shipped version of a framework file is replaced, listed under `replaced`, and afterwards byte-identical to the current plugin's copy
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 50–53 ("replaces the old version (`replaced`)"); §Decision lines 103–105
criteria.evidence: `REBASE_RESULT` line with the path under `replaced`; sha256 of the file before (the old release's bytes) and after (equal to the plugin render's)

criteria.statement: A vendored framework file already byte-identical to the plugin's copy is left alone: counted in `unchanged`, never listed as added or replaced, and its bytes and mtime are not touched
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 39 ("copies with byte comparison"); §Decision lines 80–81, 171 (`unchanged` is a count)
criteria.evidence: `REBASE_RESULT` line showing the file's category with a non-zero `unchanged` and the path in none of the lists; `stat` (mtime, size) and sha256 of that file before and after the run, equal

criteria.statement: After one `--rebase` call, the target's `.claude/` framework tree matches what the plugin installs, across every component kind (commands, agents, hooks, hook libs, hook prompts, workflows, libs, contracts, skills, framework rules): every difference left is a reported conflict, a preserved user file, an owner-governed rule or `settings.json`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 42–43 ("does all of that in one call"); §Decision lines 75–81 ("its output is, by construction, what the plugin installs ... tree against tree"), 151–155 (the component kinds)
criteria.evidence: `diff -rq` of the target's `.claude/` against a fresh ordinary scaffold of the same plugin into an empty directory, every remaining line accounted for by the result's `conflicts`/`preserved` lists, the six owner-governed rules or `settings.json`

criteria.statement: On the aged fixture, the retired file present in the target is deleted and listed under `removed`
criteria.evidence: `REBASE_RESULT` line with the path under `removed`; `ls` / `test -e` of that path after the run showing it absent

criteria.statement: A retired entry of each listed kind present in a target — a command, a hook, a `hooks/lib/` file, a `hooks/prompts/` file, a skill folder, and a directory entry (`hooks/permitter/`) — is removed by one `--rebase` call
criteria.evidence: Fixture holding one entry of each kind; `REBASE_RESULT` listing each under `removed` in its category; listing after the run showing none of the six present

criteria.statement: A file in the target that is neither shipped by the plugin nor on the retired list (the aged fixture's user agent) is kept byte-identical and listed under `preserved`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 53–54 ("keeps the user agent (`preserved`)"); §Decision lines 119–121 ("removes a file only when it is listed there ... a user's own file can never be deleted by inference")
criteria.evidence: `REBASE_RESULT` line with the user agent's path under `agents.preserved`; sha256 of the file before and after, equal

criteria.statement: The retired list is one data file the engine reads, and a test fails when it falls out of step: when a name in `rebase-project.md`'s retired tables or retired-hooks paragraph is missing from it, or when a path on it is still shipped by the plugin
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 44–45 ("a test holds them equal to the data file"); §Decision lines 115, 121–124
criteria.evidence: Jest transcript of the retired-list test passing on the current tree, plus two transcripts of it failing on a scratch copy: one with a table name deleted from the data file, one with a currently-shipped path added to it

criteria.statement: On the aged fixture, the user's own hook registration in `settings.json` is still present, on its original event, after `--rebase`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change line 54 ("keeps the user hook registration")
criteria.evidence: `jq` extract of the merged `settings.json` `hooks` showing the user registration on its event; the result's `settings` entry

criteria.statement: After the merge, the ensemble-owned part of `settings.json`'s `hooks` equals the plugin default's `hooks`, and a registration pointing at a retired hook (on any event) or at a manifest hook registered on the wrong event is gone
criteria.evidence: Fixture `settings.json` holding a retired-hook registration and a manifest hook on the wrong event; `jq` of the merged `hooks` with user registrations filtered out compared to the plugin default's `hooks` (equal), and a grep showing the retired hook's filename absent

criteria.statement: User hook registrations are compared as whole registrations, never by filename: a user command naming a file that shares a manifest hook's name at another path (`scripts/formatter.sh`) is carried forward on its own event and matcher group, after the plugin's groups, in its original order
criteria.evidence: Fixture with two user registrations, one at `scripts/<manifest-hook-name>`, on one event in a known order; `jq` of the merged event's list showing both present, after the plugin groups, order kept

criteria.statement: Every non-hooks `settings.json` key survives the merge: a key only in the plugin is added, a key present locally keeps its local value, and a new nested plugin key inside a local object is added beside the local values
criteria.evidence: Fixture `settings.json` with a changed local value, a missing plugin key and a local object lacking a nested plugin key; `jq` comparison of the merged file (with `refreshed_at` and `rebased_at` removed) against the expected values

criteria.statement: A `settings.json` key whose local and plugin values disagree in shape (one an object, the other not) is reported as a conflict and its local value kept; a `hooks` value (or an event's value) of the wrong shape is reported and `settings.json` is not written
criteria.evidence: Two fixture runs: one with a type-mismatched key (result `settings.conflicts` naming it; local value unchanged in the file), one with a malformed `hooks` (result saying the file was not written; sha256 of `settings.json` unchanged)

criteria.statement: A settings fixture whose merged `hooks` block would hold fewer registrations than the plugin default's is not written, and the result says why
criteria.evidence: `REBASE_RESULT` (or `guard` mode output) showing `refused` with the counts; sha256 of the target's `settings.json` before and after, equal

criteria.statement: A settings fixture whose merged `hooks` block would hold fewer prompt-type entries than the plugin default's is not written, and the result says why
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 59–60 ("registration or prompt count"); §Decision lines 144–146
criteria.evidence: As FS-14, with a crafted block that keeps the registration count but loses the prompt-type entry

criteria.statement: On the aged fixture, the owner-edited framework file is listed under `conflicts` (with a reason) and left byte-identical
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 54–55 ("reports the owner-edited file under `conflicts` and leaves it byte-identical"); §Decision lines 103–105
criteria.evidence: `REBASE_RESULT` line with the path and a reason under its category's `conflicts`; sha256 of the file before and after, equal

criteria.statement: The engine prints one machine-readable result: the last line of stdout is `REBASE_RESULT ` followed by one JSON object with `mode`, `preserveAll`, a `categories` object whose every entry carries `added`, `replaced`, `removed`, `preserved`, `conflicts` (lists) and `unchanged` (a count), a `settings` entry with the same six plus `counts`, `written`, `refused`, and a `steps` entry
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 42–44 ("prints a JSON result"); §Decision lines 165–171
criteria.evidence: Captured stdout of a `--rebase` run; `tail -n1` of it parsed by `jq` after stripping the prefix, exit 0, with a key listing showing each named field

criteria.statement: `--rebase --dry-run` on the aged fixture prints the same lists an apply run would and writes nothing: `git status --porcelain` stays empty and every file's bytes and mode are unchanged
criteria.evidence: Before/after listing of every path under the fixture with sha256 and octal mode (equal); `git status --porcelain` output (empty); the dry-run result's lists diffed against those of a subsequent apply on a copy (equal), `mode` reading `dry-run`

criteria.statement: Each of the six owner-governed rules (constitution.md, stack.md, process.md, verification.md, design.md, ship.md) is left byte-identical by the engine in every mode — apply, dry-run and preserve-all — including the aged fixture's owner-filled `verification.md`
criteria.cites: §Intended Change lines 51–56 ("leaves all six owner-governed rules byte-identical"); §Decision lines 156–157 ("excluded in every mode")
criteria.evidence: sha256 of the six files in `.claude/rules/` before and after each of the three runs, equal; none of the six names appearing in any result list

criteria.statement: `--refresh` on a tree holding a retired file leaves that file in place
criteria.evidence: Transcript of `--refresh` on such a tree; `test -e` of the retired path after it, present

criteria.statement: `--refresh` keeps its never-create, never-delete contract and its existing tests stay green
criteria.cites: §Decision lines 72–73 ("NOT a change to `--refresh`"); §Grounding lines 208–209 (`refresh_project` "Must not change"); §Open Questions line 250 ("`--refresh` keeps never-create/never-delete")
criteria.evidence: `bats packages/core/scripts/scaffold-project.test.sh` transcript with 0 failures; a `--refresh` on a tree missing a component directory, with a listing after it showing the directory still absent

criteria.statement: A second `--rebase` on the first run's output reports empty `added`, `replaced` and `removed` in every category, and leaves the tree byte-identical except `settings.json`'s `refreshed_at` and `rebased_at`
criteria.evidence: Second run's `REBASE_RESULT` with every `added`/`replaced`/`removed` empty; sha256 listing of the tree after run 1 and after run 2, equal except `settings.json`, whose `jq` with those two keys deleted is equal

criteria.statement: Under `--preserve-all`, agents and skills only gain new files; commands, hooks, hook libs, hook prompts, workflows, libs and contracts are replaced when they differ; framework rules are preserved; nothing is removed; in `settings.json` the `hooks` block is regenerated with retired registrations dropped, absent keys are added and no other existing value changes
criteria.evidence: `--rebase --preserve-all` on the aged fixture plus a differing agent and a differing command: result with every `removed` empty, the differing agent unchanged (sha256), the differing command replaced, the retired file still present, `settings.json` compared as in FS-10/FS-12

criteria.statement: After an apply run, every manifest hook is executable, agent skill preloads are re-injected (conflicted agents excluded), the git-files and records-cutover steps have run, and the version is stamped last, each reported under `steps`
criteria.evidence: `ls -l` of `.claude/hooks/` showing the execute bit on each manifest hook; `steps` object from the result; `jq .ensemble` of `settings.json` showing `rebased_at`; grep of a non-conflicted agent showing its preload block

criteria.statement: A file the engine adds takes the plugin source's mode (not 0600), and a file it replaces keeps its prior mode
criteria.evidence: `stat -f %Lp` (or `stat -c %a`) of an added file and its source, equal; of a replaced file before and after, equal

criteria.statement: The engine adds no library skill the target did not already have installed
criteria.cites: §Decision lines 76–79 ("so no library skill is added that the target does not have")
criteria.evidence: Listing of the target's `.claude/skills/` before and after a `--rebase`, the only new folders being framework skills shipped by the plugin

criteria.statement: `--rebase` combined with another scaffold mode is refused
criteria.evidence: Transcript of `--rebase --refresh` (and one other mode) exiting non-zero with an error message, the target unchanged
